newsitem.title: USA: FORT WORTH OFFERS PROPERTY TAX CUTS IN NEW BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: FORT WORTH OFFERS PROPERTY TAX CUTS IN NEW BUDGET.

text.p: Fort Worth's city manager on Tuesday presented a proposed $566.3 million budget for 1997-98, up 4.92 percent from this year, and called for a reduction in property tax rates.
City Manager Bob Terrell proposed cutting the city's property tax from 95 cents per $100 appraised valuation to 92.75 cents per $100.
Terrell, who presented the package at a meeting of the city council, said the tax roll has increased 5.7 percent this year and sales taxes revenues also grew 6.9 percent.

He proposed setting up a new pay scale allowing employees to enter higher pay ranges and said that those who do not benefit from that plan would receive up to a four percent general pay increase with an additional two percent tied to performance-based increases.
The budget allocates more money for street repairs, new playgrounds and two new fire stations as well as technological improvements for branch libraries.
If approved, the proposal would bring property tax rate cuts for the third straight year.
"Next year's budget plan has been formulated without compromising any of the city's financial policies. Fund balances are projected to remain at recommended levels," Terrell said.
But he said wastewater rates would have to be raised 6.2 percent because of various federal and state requirements related to environmental protection.
